patches.title: Split fused tool-call arguments into separate calls
patches.symptom: Tool call "<name>": Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position N — Received arguments:\n{...}{...}
patches.rootCause: The relay can stream two tool calls into one index. @earendil-works/pi-ai parseToolCallArguments (dist/utils/json-parse.js) receives the concatenation, throws LlmError(MALFORMED_RESPONSE), and @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop re-throws because MALFORMED_RESPONSE is not in the default retryableCodes. Measured at dsh-llm-pi-ai/lib/index.js:1656 and confirmed upstream in deepseek-harness discussion #4427.
limits: cannot recover a call whose tail was cut by max-tokens (finish.reason.kind === length)
does not fix the relay or adapter that assigned one index to two calls
does not reorder or rename calls; the first call keeps the original id
cannot attribute which upstream stage glued the objects; it only sees the assembled text

patches.title: A rescue must be provable, attributable and atomic
patches.symptom: A call split out of fused arguments runs with an empty or wrong tool name, a repaired finish replays without replayState, or a block-end repair is committed before a later block of the same stream is rejected
patches.rootCause: Repair-stream used to commit each block-end repair as it arrived, kept only the last tool name seen on an index, and emitted {kind:"stop"} without the adapter replayState. None of these break the JSON proof, so P-0001 called them repaired while the runtime could still dispatch the wrong call.
limits: cannot prove the atomic-commit path live on this host: the measured adapter never emits block-end for a tool call
proves downstream acceptance of a synthesized block-start only on the finish path; an adapter that closes blocks itself is still unmeasured (BS-11)
treats a tool name that arrives twice with different values as unrepairable, so a legitimate adapter bug stays a failure
leaves the verdict vocabulary untouched: until P-0003 every rejection was counted as fused, so a non-fusion syntax error read as degraded (BS-12, closed by P-0003)

patches.title: A refusal must be observable, and a withdrawal must not read as a repair
patches.symptom: A stream whose only defect is plain bad JSON reports "repair incomplete" (degraded), and a proven repair that was withdrawn is indistinguishable from a fusion that could never be split
patches.rootCause: RemedyMonitor.recordRejected incremented fused and unrepaired for every rejection, whatever its code (packages/plugin/src/repair-stream.ts:122-126 in 0.2.0). A refusal that never proved a fusion therefore inflated fused, which both hid quiet streams behind degraded and erased the difference between "we declined" and "we could not". Left open as BS-12 because fixing it touches the verdict counters.
limits: does not change the four verdict states or their order: refused and withdrawn are reported, never judged
cannot express "observed, refused, and correctly not repaired" in a state name; only the counter row carries it
does not migrate old journal lines, which keep the six-field counter shape
proves refused and fused on the budget-refusal path only; a live stream that moves withdrawn is still unmeasured

patches.title: A bare value after a member key must be resealed, or refused — never guessed
patches.symptom: A tool call fails with `Unexpected token 'c'` or `Unexpected end of JSON input` because the model wrote a program, not a JSON string, after `"code":`; the turn is killed with MALFORMED_RESPONSE and nothing is repaired
patches.rootCause: The adapter assembles the argument text from deltas and hands it to JSON.parse. When the model emits a bare, unquoted multi-line blob as one member value, the text is neither a fusion (one object was intended) nor recoverable by splitting, so P-0001 refuses it as `single-object` and the call is never dispatched (packages/core/src/toolcall-repair.ts:124-141 in 0.3.1).
limits: reseals only when exactly one member value proves: two possible resealings is refused as ambiguous, never chosen
never touches a truncated call: a cut tail is missing bytes, not a missing quote
does not repair a duplicate key, a doubled colon, a missing closing brace, or an illegal escape: those are refusals by design
keeps the call id, so no synthetic identity is created and the stream budget is untouched
the ninth counter is optional in the type on purpose: a 0.3.x artifact has no `resealed` field and must render exactly as it did

patches.title: A scan must read the log it is pointed at, and a redaction must see every path shape
patches.symptom: `dsh-remedy scan <session.v4.jsonl.zstd>` reported 0 attempts and one unreadable line per compressed byte, and artifacts that cited a session file carried the account name in three shapes the redactor could not match
patches.rootCause: cmdScan read a multi-frame zstd session with readFileSync(file, "utf8") instead of the decompressSessionLog reader the plugin already ships (packages/plugin/src/cli.ts:236 in 0.3.2), and core/redact.ts matched only a single-backslash C:\Users\<name>, so a JSON-escaped path, a slashed path and a DSH session directory named after the home path all passed through.
limits: reports a filtered scan as before_since instead of guessing; an unstamped event inside a window is unreadable, never assumed in the window
one undecompressable file is a failures line and exit 3, not a silent zero
does not deduplicate the same repair seen by both the journal and the session file
matches a home path only when the directory starts with a drive letter; another workspace spelling is unmeasured

patches.title: A scan that counts only the repairable turns is not a fault map
patches.symptom: `dsh-remedy scan` reported 44 fusion failures out of 287 finished turns on this host: the 88 turns that died on `max-tokens` (31% of all turns) and the 36 that died on `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT` were not counted anywhere, so the biggest failure classes were invisible in the one report meant to map them
patches.rootCause: packages/plugin/src/session-scan.ts read `data.reason` on `turn/end` and returned early twice, on `kind !== "error"` and on `code !== "MALFORMED_RESPONSE"`. That filter is correct for "can this layer repair it?" and wrong for "how did the turn end?": the report carried the filter into the map.
limits: a census is reported, never promoted into a finding: the scan exit code still turns on fused_calls and fusion_failures, so 88 truncated turns do not make every scripted scan fail
truncated turns stay unfixed: a cut tail is missing bytes, not a missing quote, and 0 of 88 truncated turns could be tied to a buffered call
`fusion_failures` keeps its exact meaning (`MALFORMED_RESPONSE` turns only), so an older artifact reads the same as it did before
an error code is counted under the name the adapter emitted; the report is redacted before it leaves the CLI, and the code vocabulary is a closed set of short identifiers
a `reason.kind` this census does not know is left uncounted rather than given a bucket of its own

patches.title: A copy channel that reports "exited null" cannot be repaired
patches.symptom: the two longest outward files, README.md and CHANGELOG.md, could not be regenerated at all: every attempt printed `copy_with_agy: agy exited null` and nothing else, so the same six words had to be retried from scratch with no way to learn what went wrong between attempts
patches.rootCause: scripts/copy_with_agy.mjs put the whole request on one Windows command line. Once the fact pack grew the request measured 35509 characters for changelog and 33530 for readme against the 32767 character cap, so spawnSync failed before agy ever started: run.error.code was ENAMETOOLONG and run.status was null. A generation that instead outlived the 600000 ms spawn timeout was killed the same way, with the same null status, so two different faults printed one unreadable line
limits: the channel does not retry a failed generation across transports: it picks one transport from the request length and reports whatever went wrong, so the operator still re-runs a failure by hand
the timeout is raised to half an hour, not removed: an agy that hangs is still killed and still named as a timeout
a transport failure is diagnosed, not repaired — a refusal, a missing model and a missing binary each keep their own message
the fact pack is not shortened to fit the cap, so the stdin path stays the normal path and the argv path only serves the smallest briefs

patches.title: A byte budget that no script checks is a suggestion
patches.symptom: the byte budget was written down in prose and crossed three consecutive times before anyone noticed: the plugin total reached 55815 bytes after P-0005, 64539 after P-0004 and 70389 on the first P-0006 attempt, and each crossing was found by hand after the patch had already been built, tested and packed
patches.rootCause: the caps lived only in the fact pack and README.md. Nothing in scripts/ read them, so a patch that crossed a line stayed green through 189 tests and five gates, and the structural split that fixed it happened afterwards. grepping scripts/ for the ceiling returned no hits, which is the whole defect: the number had no mechanism
limits: the gate measures the emitted plugin only: core does not load at startup, so the ceiling protects what is loaded there
it does not shrink anything; the measured numbers stay what they were when the gate was written
it does not measure dist/*.d.ts, which is paid at build time rather than load time
it cannot decide how to split a file that crosses a cap — it only refuses the crossing, so the structural fix stays a human decision
